entities.summary: Tacitus, a Roman historian and politician, played a pivotal role in shaping our understanding of the Roman Empire's decline and fall. Born in Rome, Tacitus rose through the ranks of Roman politics, eventually becoming a senator and a key figure in the Roman Senate. His most notable works, the Annals and the Histories, provide a wealth of information on the Roman Empire's internal politics, military campaigns, and social dynamics. Tacitus' writings are considered some of the greatest Roman historians by modern scholars, offering a unique perspective on the era. His legacy extends beyond his writings, influencing the development of historical scholarship and the study of ancient Rome.
